USD.catalyst: The US Dollar index holds above key moving averages at 102.23, outperforming G10 peers over the past week (+0.92%) as markets reprice Federal Reserve terminal rate expectations upward following hot October consumer price data. Fed holds at 4.00%. Foreign central bank intervention in Asian and emerging markets, including reported liquidity actions by the State Bank of Vietnam and Bank Indonesia, underscores broadening dollar demand pressures across cross-border funding channels. DXY maintains technical support above its 20-day (101.89) and 50-day (101.37) moving averages as institutional focus turns to a slate of upcoming Fed speaker appearances.

GBP.catalyst: Sterling displays modest daily resilience across G10 crosses (+0.06%), supported by persistent UK core inflation risks despite downward revisions to near-term growth trajectories. The National Institute of Economic and Social Research warned that UK inflation may remain above the 2% target through 2030 due to sticky wage growth, preserving a persistent yield advantage in forward swaps. Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey’s recent remarks defending central bank independence precede a crucial domestic data slate, highlighted by UK gross domestic product data due on Thursday. Against the dollar, the pound trades just below its 20-day moving average of 1.3364 and 50-day average of 1.3357 as markets gauge the likelihood of another BoE pause against Fed repricing.

EUR.catalyst: The euro remains soft across G10 crosses, consolidating below its 20-day and 50-day moving averages against the dollar as sovereign spread pressures resurface across European bond markets. Sentiment is constrained after European Central Bank Chief Economist Philip Lane signaled that the bar for directional rate guidance remains high, leaving markets uncertain over upcoming policy easing steps. Concurrently, Eurogroup finance ministers convened on November 9 to deliberate potential successors to ECB President Christine Lagarde, with former Bank of Spain Governor Pablo Hernández de Cos featured prominently among candidates. Speculative positioning remains heavily defensive, with CFTC data indicating leveraged funds hold net-short exposure of −104,030 contracts amid sovereign spread divergence between core and peripheral debt.

JPY.catalyst: The Japanese yen faces broad G10 underperformance (−0.18% over the past week), weighed down by a 265-basis-point short-term rate differential between SOFR at 3.88% and TONA at 1.23%. While newly installed Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi stated she expects the Bank of Japan to implement suitable monetary policy to sustainably reach its 2% inflation goal, the central bank’s measured stance leaves the currency vulnerable near historical lows. Japanese domestic corporate sentiment remains solid, with the Reuters Tankan manufacturing gauge rising to +27, its strongest print in over five years driven by semiconductor demand. Nevertheless, the currency is testing critical levels above 158.00 against the greenback, prompting heightened trader scrutiny over potential Ministry of Finance physical currency intervention.

AUD.catalyst: The Australian dollar posted an intraday rebound (+0.17% composite day) despite lingering macro headwinds stemming from tighter domestic credit conditions. Third-quarter Australian investor home lending plunged 32% following aggressive Reserve Bank of Australia tightening and local tax curbs, curbing broader domestic demand projections. The currency remains structurally depressed against the US dollar, trading below its 20-day moving average of 0.6984 and 50-day moving average of 0.7037 after hot US inflation figures triggered technical breakdowns below key horizontal support at 0.6905. Australian rate expectations remain steady after the RBA’s recent policy hike was treated as a cautious, data-dependent adjustment.

CAD.catalyst: The Canadian dollar underperformed across G10 counterparts (−0.75% over the past week), pressured by softer crude oil export values and diverging North American economic momentum. Although Bank of Canada Governing Council minutes highlighted that officials still see a possible need to hike interest rates further if persistent underlying price pressures linger, third-quarter labor contraction with unemployment climbing to 6.7% has dampened policy conviction. The currency trades on the defensive against the greenback, positioned well above its 20-day moving average of 1.4060 and 200-day moving average of 1.3897. Markets await the publication of full BoC policy deliberations alongside upcoming Canadian CPI prints to assess whether policy divergence against the Federal Reserve will widen.

CHF.catalyst: The Swiss franc lagged G10 peers with a −0.72% composite weekly decline, softening as safe-haven premia recede and lower inflation dynamics take hold. The Swiss National Bank maintained its policy rate unchanged at its prior quarterly meeting, signaling that direct FX interventions to restrain nominal currency strength remain unnecessary while energy prices fluctuate. Trading against the US dollar places the pair above its 20-day moving average of 0.8238 and 50-day moving average of 0.8235, reinforced by a bullish daily technical engulfing expansion. Domestic focus is locked on whether the SNB will maintain an accommodative bias given the sub-2% domestic inflation backdrop ahead of the central bank’s December quarterly rate review.

NZD.catalyst: The New Zealand dollar leads G10 performance on a one-week horizon (+1.06%), staging an extended recovery after political uncertainty narrowed following domestic coalition developments. BBH noted the ruling center-right coalition secured a narrow parliamentary majority, providing clarity on fiscal and tax policy agendas even as Citi pared back expectations for further Reserve Bank of New Zealand policy tightening. The RBNZ’s prior signal ending its aggressive easing cycle has supported two-year interest rate swaps, which lifted to 2.6653% as swap markets reduced the implied probability of imminent rate cuts. Against the dollar, the currency is consolidating below its 20-day moving average of 0.5640, finding support as global risk appetite steadies.

NOK.catalyst: The Norwegian krone remains the weakest performer in the G10 complex over the past week (−1.85%), burdened by recent retreats in Brent crude prices and broad US dollar strength. While Norges Bank previously kept its benchmark policy rate unchanged while leaving the door open to future tightening if inflation lingers, the loss of export revenue support has offset monetary policy firmness. Against the dollar, the exchange rate posted a wide-range expansion above its 20-day moving average of 9.354 and 200-day moving average of 9.488, lifting to 9.506. Institutional desks are focused on upcoming Norwegian consumer inflation data to gauge whether Norges Bank will be forced into an extended hold.

SEK.catalyst: The Swedish krona trades with modest weekly losses (−0.37%), hovering around 10.99 against the euro as regional fiscal and bond market volatility counteracts domestic central bank support. Sweden’s Riksbank lifted its policy rate by 25 basis points to 2.00% at its November gathering, with Riksbank officials subsequently signaling the possibility of another hike at the upcoming December meeting. While higher European defense spending commitments and Riksbank policy tightening provide underlying fundamental anchors, the krona remains exposed to broader European economic deceleration. Against the greenback, the exchange rate trades near its 20-day moving average of 9.875, pending fresh Scandinavian industrial and inflation data.
